angle: In Simcoe County a hot tub or sauna is four-season equipment: it earns its keep on January nights after the ski hill, on damp April weekends at the lake, and on every evening a Highway 400 commuter finally gets home.

hot-tub.intro: Long winters, deep snow and a cottage an hour up the road shape how people around here buy. Every Jacuzzi, Nordic, Aquasolus and Wellness Shop Ontario tub below is priced exactly as it sits on our Bryne Drive floor.
body: Barrie sits in the snow belt, and the squalls that roll off Georgian Bay can drop a foot overnight on a cover that has to hold it. We recommend a cover lifter on every tub we deliver here, and we help you place the tub so the snow you clear off the deck does not land on the cabinet. A tub running at full temperature through a Simcoe County winter needs real insulation and a tight cover; the difference shows up on your February hydro bill. Right now every new 2026 Jacuzzi in stock is 20% off in our Red Tag inventory clearance, not combinable with other offers.

Lots here range widely. South Barrie, Innisfil and Bradford new builds usually have a tight rear yard, a six foot gate and a basement panel close to the back wall, which makes for a straightforward dolly delivery and a short electrical run. Older homes in Allandale and the east end often have mature trees and a narrower side yard, so we measure before we quote. Cottage and waterfront properties on Lake Simcoe or Georgian Bay are a different job: sloped lots, seasonal roads and long distances to the hydro panel. Our crews handle all of it, including crane lifts over a cottage roof.

Who buys here: families in the subdivisions along Mapleview and Big Bay Point Road who want a seven seat J-385 or J-485 the kids can pile into, commuters who sit in Highway 400 traffic and want the J-335 running when they pull in, and cottage owners who take a Nordic Retreat All-In-110V up north because it plugs into what the cottage already has. Skiers heading home from Horseshoe Valley or Blue Mountain are our January regulars. If your water comes from a well, tell us; we set up water care differently for hard or high iron water than for Barrie municipal supply.

faq.q: Can I run a hot tub at a cottage with only 100 amp service?
faq.a: Usually yes. The Nordic Sport All-In-110V and Retreat All-In-110V plug into a dedicated standard outlet and heat more slowly, which suits a cottage used on weekends. If you want a full 240V Jacuzzi at the lake, have an ESA licensed electrician do a load calculation first; many cottages have room for a 50 amp GFCI circuit once the baseboard heaters are accounted for.

faq.q: When is the best time of year to have a tub delivered to a cottage?
faq.a: Late spring after the half load season lifts, or fall before the seasonal roads close. Spring load restrictions on county and township roads limit what a delivery truck can carry for several weeks, so we schedule around them. Winter deliveries to plowed year round roads are fine and common in Barrie itself.

faq.q: How much snow can a hot tub cover take?
faq.a: The covers on the Jacuzzi and Nordic tubs we sell are built to carry a normal snow load, but a wet Georgian Bay squall can pile on more weight than any cover should sit under for days. Brush it off when it gets deep, the same as you would a gazebo roof. A cover lifter makes that easier and keeps the cover out of the snowbank when you get in.

faq.q: Does well water change how I look after the tub?
faq.a: Yes. Well water in Oro-Medonte, Essa and rural Innisfil often runs hard with iron or manganese, which stains shells and clouds water if you fill straight from the hose. We recommend a pre-filter on the fill hose and a metal sequestering treatment at start-up. On Barrie or Orillia municipal water the routine is simpler, and we will set you up with the right test strips either way.

faq.q: Will the tub stay warm if we lose power in a winter storm?
faq.a: A full foam insulated tub with the cover on holds usable heat for a day or more in a typical outage, and the water will not freeze for considerably longer. For cottages that sit empty, ask us about freeze protection and the SmartTub app on the J-400 and J-500 series so you get a temperature alert on your phone. A small generator can run the circulation pump if outages are common on your road.

swim-spa.intro: A swim spa gives you a lap lane you can use in February, which matters in a region where the outdoor pool season is barely three months and the lake stays cold until July. Every model here is a heated, year round installation.
body: Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay give this area a lot of swimmers and paddlers, and most of them lose their training water from Thanksgiving to Victoria Day. A swim spa closes that gap. Triathletes and masters swimmers around here use the 19 foot Jacuzzi J-19 PowerPro for its current, families in Innisfil pick the 13 foot J-13 PowerPlay for its eight seats, and retirees who want gentle resistance walking choose the 12 foot J-12 Flow at $30,695. None of them need to drive to a pool at six in the morning through a snow squall.

Winter running cost is the question we hear most from Simcoe County buyers, and it comes down to insulation, cover and placement. Site the spa out of the prevailing west wind if you can, with the long side against a fence or the house, and keep the cover sealed when nobody is in it. The dual temperature models, the Jacuzzi J-19DT PowerPro at $60,895 and the SwimLife SwimExpert DualStream 19 at $56,095, let you keep the swim end cooler and the hot tub end at soaking temperature, which is more efficient than heating one large body of water for both jobs.

Almost every swim spa we deliver in this region goes in by crane, and in the subdivisions of south Barrie, Innisfil and Bradford that usually means a lift over the house from the street on delivery day. On larger rural and lakefront lots we can sometimes back the truck to the pad. Either way you need a reinforced concrete pad or an engineered deck, and the town or township will want to see a permit and pool fencing, so check the requirements where you live early. We book the crane and coordinate with your electrician and contractor.

faq.q: Can I install a swim spa at a lakefront cottage?
faq.a: Yes, and it is a popular choice on Lake Simcoe where the water is cold and weedy for much of the season. The main constraints are hydro capacity, since a swim spa needs a dedicated 50 or 60 amp circuit, and crane access on a treed waterfront lot. Shoreline setbacks are enforced by the township and sometimes the conservation authority, so confirm placement before you pour a pad.

faq.q: Should I sink the swim spa into the ground or build a deck around it?
faq.a: Partial in-ground installs look best and make getting in easy, but the frost line here is deep and the excavation needs proper drainage and a vault you can still access for service. A raised deck built to the rim of the spa is the more common choice in Barrie backyards and avoids the groundwater problems that come with our spring thaw. We can share drawings your contractor can work from.

faq.q: Do I need to winterize a swim spa?
faq.a: No. A swim spa is built to run all year and it is easier on the equipment to keep it heated than to drain it. If you are away for weeks at a time, lower the set point and leave it running; the connected Jacuzzi models will alert you if anything changes. Draining is only for a cottage that loses hydro over winter, and we can walk you through that.

faq.q: How does a swim spa handle heavy snow?
faq.a: The hard cover carries a normal load, but a swim spa cover is large, so sweep it after a big squall rather than letting a week of snow sit on it. Place the spa where roof runoff and drifting will not bury one side. Owners who use theirs daily in winter tell us the routine is a two minute broom and a quick walk on a cleared path.

faq.q: Which swim spa is best for a family with young kids?
faq.a: The 13 foot Jacuzzi J-13 PowerPlay at $33,195 with eight seats, or the 12 foot J-12 Flow at $30,695, gives you a shallow, warm play area with a gentler current than the PowerPro lane. Both fit a standard subdivision backyard. Older kids on swim teams outgrow them and want the stronger current of a 14 or 16 foot PowerActive or PowerPro.

sauna.intro: Six months of real winter make this good sauna country. Clearlight infrared cabins go in a basement or garage and plug in; Serenity cedar saunas sit outside beside the snowbank the way they do in Finland.
body: The outdoor sauna has deep roots in this part of Ontario, and a Serenity cedar sauna on a rural lot in Oro-Medonte or a Georgian Bay waterfront in Midland fits the landscape. The Serenity Sauna at $17,495 seats a family; the Serenity Mini at $14,995 suits a couple or a smaller cottage lot. Heaters are sold separately, and the choice matters here: a wood burning heater needs no hydro at all, which is exactly what an off grid or hydro limited cottage wants, while an electric heater on a dedicated 240V circuit is the easy option for a Barrie backyard.

Indoors, Clearlight infrared is what commuters and shift workers around here buy for recovery after long drives and long days. A Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 fits a basement corner in a south Barrie or Innisfil two storey and runs off a standard outlet, and right now it comes with the Chill Tubs Essential bundle at no charge, so you get the hot and cold contrast in one purchase. Townhome and condo owners in the downtown and waterfront buildings choose the Sanctuary 1 at $10,495 because it fits through a standard door and assembles in an afternoon.

Outdoor saunas need a level base above grade so spring melt does not sit against the cedar, and in the snow belt a small roof overhang or a covered walkway from the house is worth planning. Site the door away from the prevailing wind and leave room for a cold plunge or a snowbank beside it, because that is half the point. The cabin is delivered in panels and assembled on site by our crew, usually in a day. Check with your township on accessory structure setbacks before you pick the spot; the rules differ between Barrie, Innisfil and the rural townships.

faq.q: Can I heat an outdoor sauna with wood at a cottage?
faq.a: Yes, and many cottage owners on Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay do exactly that because it costs nothing in hydro and works during a power outage. A wood burning heater needs a proper chimney and clearances, and your insurer may want to know about it, so tell them. Firewood is easy to find around here and a sauna burns far less than a woodstove.

faq.q: How do I keep an outdoor sauna dry through the spring thaw?
faq.a: Set it on a gravel bed with patio stones or a small deck so meltwater drains away from the base, and leave a gap between the cabin and any fence for airflow. Cedar handles moisture well but standing water at the sill will shorten its life. Open the door and vent after each session, especially in the damp weeks of March and April.

faq.q: Will an infrared sauna heat up in an unheated garage in January?
faq.a: It will, but slowly, and the cabin loses heat to a cold room. Most owners in this climate put the Clearlight in a basement or a finished room where the ambient temperature stays above about 15 degrees. If the garage is your only option, insulate the space or plan on a longer warm-up through the winter.

faq.q: Which sauna works in a townhome or condo?
faq.a: The Clearlight Sanctuary 1 or Sanctuary 2 is the usual pick in the townhomes off Mapleview and the condos downtown and along the waterfront. Both plug into a standard outlet, need no venting and sit on any flat floor. Check with your condo board about assembly and weight limits before you order, and measure the doorway and any turns in the hallway.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a Serenity sauna delivered and built?
faq.a: Lead times vary with cedar grade and heater choice, so ask for the current timeline when you order. Late spring through fall is the busy season for outdoor builds; winter builds are possible on a cleared, level base. Our crew assembles the panelled cabin on site, and your electrician connects the heater afterward if you chose electric.

hot-tub.small: A small tub is the cottage tub here. The Nordic Sport All-In-110V at $7,295 and Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 run off a dedicated standard outlet, so a lake place with an older 100 amp panel and electric baseboards can still have a hot tub without a service upgrade. The Jacuzzi J-315 at $18,795 and J-404L at $25,195 are the pick for a couple in a downtown townhome or a retirement bungalow in Alcona where two people soak most nights and the yard is small. Both fit through a standard gate on a dolly.
hot-tub.medium: Five and six seat tubs are the everyday Simcoe County backyard tub. The Jacuzzi J-335 at $21,995 is the one we sell most to commuter families in the new builds along Mapleview and in Innisfil; the J-235 at $16,295 does the same job for less. The Aquasolus The Eden at $13,995 comes with White Glove delivery and setup included, which matters on a rural lot. If you want the SmartTub app to warm the tub from the car on the 400, look at the J-435 floor model at $24,995 or the J-408L at $29,995.
hot-tub.large: Seven seats and up is what the cottage crowd and the big blended families buy. The Jacuzzi J-509 at $39,595 with 76 jets is the flagship for a large new build or a lakefront place where the whole family gathers on a long weekend. The J-495 floor model at $31,395 gives you nine seats for far less, and the J-385 at $26,595 or J-245 at $16,295 are the sensible family picks. On Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe properties a big tub almost always goes in by crane, so we survey the lot first and price the lift into the quote.

productNotes.swim-spa: Swim spas in this region are bought by two groups: swimmers and triathletes who lose Lake Simcoe from October to June, and families who want a pool without a pool contractor and a five month season. The Jacuzzi J-19 PowerPro at $58,995 and the SwimLife SwimExpert AquaStream 17 at $50,095 are the training choices; the J-13 PowerPlay at $33,195 and J-12 Flow at $30,695 are the family choices. All of them run through the winter, and on a deck against the house they double as a very large hot tub after skiing.
productNotes.sauna: Sauna buyers around here split cleanly. Cottage owners and rural households in Oro-Medonte, Midland and Collingwood want a Serenity cedar sauna outdoors, usually with a wood burning heater at the lake and an electric one in town. Commuters, hospital and college staff and the fitness crowd want a Clearlight Sanctuary infrared cabin in the basement for daily recovery. The Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 and Sanctuary Y at $13,995 currently include the Chill Tubs Essential bundle, which is the fastest way into a hot and cold routine without building anything outside.
productNotes.cold-plunge: Cold plunge came naturally to a region where people already jump in the lake in May. The Chill Tubs Essential Bath and Essential Pod are the entry points, the Obsidian and the Pro are the chilled, filtered units for daily use, and all four are priced in the showroom rather than online. They pair with a Serenity outdoor sauna on a rural lot or a Clearlight cabin in the basement, and they run all year on a standard outlet. Come try one on the floor; it is a different conversation once you have been in.

financing: Most of our Barrie customers finance, and the pattern is practical: a bi-weekly payment that fits alongside a mortgage on a new build in Innisfil or Bradford, or a second payment for a cottage tub that goes up the 400 in May. The Nordic Retreat All-In-110V works out from $18.62 bi-weekly and the Sport from $15.01, which for many cottage owners is less than the propane they burn on a long weekend. Approval is quick, terms are shown on every product page, and you can apply in the showroom on Bryne Drive or from home before you drive up.
showroom: The showroom is on Bryne Drive in south Barrie, just off Highway 400 at Mapleview, which puts it on the way to nearly everywhere in Simcoe County. Cottage traffic passes it on Friday afternoon and Innisfil and Bradford commuters pass it every day. Every hot tub, swim spa and sauna on the floor is heated and running, so you can sit in a J-385, feel the current in a swim spa and step into a Serenity cedar cabin on the same visit.

Bring your lot measurements, a photo of the gate and side yard, and a picture of your electrical panel if you can; with those our team can tell you on the spot whether it is a dolly or a crane job and roughly what the electrical run will cost. Cottage owners should bring the road name and whether it is plowed in winter. Wet tests are welcome by appointment, and if you are coming from Orillia, Collingwood or Midland we will make sure the models you want to compare are running when you arrive.

Innisfil.lead: Innisfil is our closest service area and one of our busiest, from the new subdivisions in Alcona to the Lake Simcoe shoreline between Big Bay Point and Gilford.
body: Housing here splits between fast growing subdivision streets in Alcona and Lefroy with tight lots and rear yards backing onto other rear yards, and older lake lots on the shore roads with mature trees and long, narrow driveways. Subdivision deliveries are usually a straightforward dolly job through a rear gate, and the panel is close. The shore properties are more often a crane lift, and if the hydro is an older service we look at a Nordic 110V or plan a service upgrade with the electrician.

Innisfil buyers are commuters who drive the 400 to Vaughan and Toronto and want the tub hot when they get home, and Lake Simcoe cottage owners who have turned a summer place into a year round home. The Jacuzzi J-335 and J-385 are the most common picks in the subdivisions. On the shoreline, where the yard is bigger and the family shows up all summer, the seven seat J-485 and the eight seat J-509 make sense. Well water is common outside the serviced areas, so ask us about fill filters.
Innisfil.drive: Take Yonge Street or Highway 400 north to Mapleview Drive, then head west to Bryne Drive; from Alcona it is about twenty minutes.

Orillia.lead: Orillia sits between Lake Couchiching and Lake Simcoe at the top of Highway 11, a forty minute run down to our Barrie showroom and a market with its own strong cottage culture.
body: The city itself has a lot of older homes near the downtown and the waterfront with deep, narrow lots and detached garages, plus newer subdivisions on the west side toward Highway 11. Older lots often mean a walk down a side yard with a dolly, or a small crane over a garage. The surrounding cottage roads on Couchiching, the Severn and the north end of Simcoe are where the bigger crane jobs are, and where seasonal road access shapes when we can deliver.

Orillia buyers include retirees who moved up from the GTA and want a comfortable six seater like the J-355 or J-435 for two people most nights, university and hospital staff who want a Clearlight infrared for recovery, and cottage families who want the biggest tub the hydro will carry. Water care differs street by street: municipal supply in town, wells and lake draw at many cottages. We stock the treatment products for both and set the tub up accordingly.
Orillia.drive: Highway 11 south becomes Highway 400 at Barrie; stay on the 400 south to the Mapleview exit and turn west to Bryne Drive, about forty minutes from downtown Orillia.

Alliston.lead: Alliston and the rest of New Tecumseth are a mix of long established town streets, farm properties and newer subdivisions filled with people who work at the Honda plant or commute south.
body: Lots in the older part of town are generous by subdivision standards, with room for a tub off a back deck and a side yard wide enough for a dolly. The newer subdivisions on the edges are tighter and the delivery is planned around the gate width and the air conditioner placement. Farm and rural properties between Alliston, Beeton and Tottenham have all the space in the world but often a long run to the panel and a well, so we plan the electrical and the water care before delivery day.

Shift workers are a big part of the Alliston market, and a tub they can use at odd hours without waking the house is the ask: a six seater like the Jacuzzi J-335 or the Aquasolus The Eden with White Glove setup included. Rural families lean to the seven seat J-385 or the Wellness Shop Ontario S104, and a Serenity outdoor cedar sauna is a natural fit on a farm lot with room and firewood to spare.
Alliston.drive: Follow Highway 89 east to Highway 400 at Cookstown, head north to the Mapleview exit and turn west; the drive from Alliston is around forty minutes in normal traffic.

Midland.lead: Midland and Penetanguishene sit on Severn Sound at the edge of Georgian Bay, in the heart of the snow belt and surrounded by some of the most popular cottage country in Ontario.
body: Waterfront and cottage properties dominate the calls we get from here: sloped lots down to the Bay, treed lanes, seasonal roads in Tiny and Tay, and hydro that was sized for a summer cabin. Crane delivery is the norm rather than the exception, and we time deliveries around spring load restrictions and fall road closures. In town, older homes on the streets above the harbour have decent yards and municipal water, which keeps the job simple.

The snow off Georgian Bay is heavier here than in Barrie, so we talk about cover lifters, roof runoff and placement before we talk about jets. Cottage owners choose the Nordic Retreat All-In-110V for a weekend place with light hydro, or a Jacuzzi J-245 or J-285 where the panel can take a 240V circuit and the whole family comes up. This is also our strongest market for a Serenity outdoor sauna with a wood burning heater, which fits the setting and works when the power goes out.
Midland.drive: Take Highway 93 south to Highway 400, continue south and exit at Mapleview, then turn west to Bryne Drive; plan on about fifty minutes from Midland harbour.

Collingwood.lead: Collingwood combines a lively downtown, the ski hills at Blue Mountain and a Georgian Bay waterfront, and hot tubs here are as much ski equipment as backyard furniture.
body: The market is unusual: chalets and townhomes near the hill that are used on winter weekends, established homes in town with mature lots, and waterfront condos and new builds along the Bay. Chalet deliveries are often crane lifts on sloped, treed lots with a driveway full of cars, and the tub has to be placed where a January dump does not bury the steps. Townhome and condo owners tend to look at a Clearlight infrared cabin or a compact tub like the J-315 that fits a small patio.

Skiers want heat fast and a tub big enough for a house full of guests, which is why the Jacuzzi J-485 and J-495 do well here, and the SmartTub app that brings the tub up to temperature before you leave the hill gets used constantly. Year round residents are often retirees and remote workers who use the tub daily and appreciate the lower running cost of a well insulated Jacuzzi. Check with the town on setbacks; Collingwood and the Blue Mountains have their own rules for accessory structures.
Collingwood.drive: Highway 26 east through Stayner brings you into north Barrie; join Highway 400 south to the Mapleview exit and turn west, roughly an hour door to door.

Wasaga Beach.lead: Wasaga Beach is a beach town that has become a year round community, with new subdivisions inland and older cottages along the Nottawasaga River and the shore of Georgian Bay.
body: Housing is a mix of small original cottages on sandy lots, retirement bungalows in the newer subdivisions off Mosley Street and River Road, and a growing number of families who moved up for the price of a house. Sandy soil makes for easy digging but calls for a properly compacted base under any pad; a tub that settles unevenly will not drain right. Many lots are flat with good access, so a dolly delivery through a side gate is more common here than in Collingwood.

The people buying here are retirees who want a five or six seater like the Jacuzzi J-325 or J-335 for daily soaks and grandchildren on weekends, and young families who came for affordability and want a full size tub without a full size price, which is where the Aquasolus The Cove at $11,995 and the Wellness Shop Ontario S104 at $15,595 come in. Lake effect snow is heavy here, so a cover lifter and a sheltered placement are part of every quote.
Wasaga Beach.drive: Take Highway 26 east or County Road 92 through Elmvale to reach Highway 400 in north Barrie, then south to Mapleview and west to Bryne Drive; about forty five minutes from the beach.

Bradford.lead: Bradford is the southern edge of our territory, a fast growing commuter town beside the Holland Marsh with its own GO station and a Highway 400 interchange at Highway 88.
body: Almost everything built in Bradford in the last fifteen years is a subdivision home on a compact lot, with a rear yard that backs onto a neighbour and a gate that is usually wide enough for a dolly but not always. We measure gates and check for air conditioner units and window wells before delivery. The older streets near downtown and the farm properties out toward the Marsh give you more room and, in the rural cases, a well and a longer electrical run.

Bradford buyers are almost all commuters, many driving to Vaughan, Newmarket or downtown Toronto every day, and the ask is a tub the family can use on weeknights without a lot of fuss: the Jacuzzi J-335 at $21,995 and J-235 at $16,295 are the two we sell most here. Households with teenagers step up to a J-385. Our Vaughan showroom is also within reach, but Barrie is the stop if you want to see the full swim spa and sauna floor on your way north.
Bradford.drive: Highway 400 north from the Highway 88 interchange to the Mapleview exit, then west to Bryne Drive; about twenty five minutes outside rush hour.

Angus.lead: Angus is a Township of Essa community on the Nottawasaga River west of Barrie, next to Base Borden, with newer subdivisions and a long history as a military family town.
body: Lots here are a mix of newer subdivision homes with modest rear yards and older properties on larger lots near the river, plus rural acreages on the concession roads toward Baxter and Thornton. Subdivision deliveries are routine dolly jobs. On the acreages the tub is often a long way from the house panel, so we get the electrician involved early, and most of those properties are on wells that run hard, which changes the start-up water care.

Military families post in and out, and they tell us they want a tub that is easy to own and easy to sell or move: the Jacuzzi J-235 and the Aquasolus The Calma are popular for that reason. Longer term residents on rural lots take the seven seat J-345 or J-365 and often add a Serenity outdoor cedar sauna where they have the space. Angus is close enough to Barrie that scheduling is simple once the pad and electrical are ready.
Angus.drive: Head east on Highway 90 into Barrie, then take Essa Road south to Bryne Drive, or hop on the 400 south one exit to Mapleview; around twenty minutes.

Oro-Medonte.lead: Oro-Medonte is the township between Barrie and Orillia, stretching from the Lake Simcoe shore at Shanty Bay and Hawkestone up to the ski hills at Horseshoe Valley and Mount St. Louis Moonstone.
body: Almost every property here is rural or waterfront: estate lots on the concession roads, lakefront homes and cottages on the shore roads, and chalets and new builds around Horseshoe Valley. Space is rarely the problem. Distance to the panel, well water and winter access are. Long driveways mean we can often bring the truck right to the pad, but sloped shore lots still need a crane. Nearly all of the township is on wells, so pre-filtering the fill water and a start-up metal treatment are standard on our deliveries here.

The ski hill neighbourhoods buy tubs for after the last run and want them big and hot: the Jacuzzi J-485 and J-495 are the fit, and the SmartTub app matters when the house sits empty midweek. Lakeshore residents, many of them retirees, prefer a six seater like the J-375 or J-445 for daily use. On the estate lots a Serenity outdoor sauna with a wood or electric heater is a common addition beside the tub, and there is room for a proper cold plunge next to both.
Oro-Medonte.drive: From Horseshoe Valley Road or the lakeshore, join Highway 11 south into Barrie, continue on Highway 400 south to Mapleview and turn west; twenty to thirty five minutes depending on where you start.

Newmarket.lead: Newmarket is a York Region town of established neighbourhoods and newer subdivisions, home to a regional hospital and a busy GO line, and the southernmost community we serve from Barrie.
body: Housing is mostly mature suburban streets with decent size lots and fenced yards, plus newer, tighter subdivisions on the edges and a growing number of townhomes near Davis Drive and Yonge Street. Older lots often have a side yard wide enough for a dolly; townhomes and the newer streets are more often a crane over the garage. Municipal water keeps water care simple, and the panel is rarely far from the back wall.

Hospital staff, commuters on the 404 and the GO, and families with kids in sports are the core buyers, and they want a tub for recovery and weeknight use: the Jacuzzi J-335 and J-355 are the usual picks, and a Clearlight Sanctuary 2 in the basement is the sauna choice. Newmarket sits between our Barrie and Vaughan showrooms; come to Bryne Drive if you are heading north anyway or want to talk through a cottage install, because a lot of Newmarket families also own a place up north.
Newmarket.drive: Take Davis Drive west to Highway 400, head north to the Mapleview exit and turn west to Bryne Drive; about thirty five minutes without traffic.
